markdown_content: ## 3D File Import & Export Presets Overview This section explains the new functionality for managing file export presets in 3D software, focusing on OBJ and FBX formats. It covers how presets improve workflow efficiency by allowing users and companies to save and quickly apply customized export settings specific to different target applications like Blender or Cinema 4D. ### Export Presets for OBJ and FBX Files A key update enables users to create and manage export presets directly from the file export dialog. When exporting, such as to OBJ format, a "Presets" option appears, allowing you to: - Set up customized export settings for specific target applications (e.g., Blender, Cinema 4D). - Save the current export settings as a preset by clicking the "Add" button, naming the preset, and saving it. - Load saved presets to quickly apply consistent export configurations. - Delete existing presets to clean up or update available options. **Procedure to Create and Use Presets:** 1. Configure export settings as needed (e.g., toggles for geometry, scale, units). 2. Click the "Add" button to save these settings as a new preset. 3. Name the preset (e.g., "Blender") and save it. 4. Presets are saved to a default folder, but you can change the save location by opening the preset folder and selecting another directory. 5. When exporting, select the desired preset from the dropdown to apply those settings instantly. 6. Presets can be deleted by selecting them and hitting the "Delete" button, followed by confirmation. Each file format (OBJ, FBX, etc.) supports its own set of presets, allowing tailored export configurations per format. This system significantly streamlines repetitive export tasks and ensures consistency across projects. --- ## Exporting and Importing DXF Files with Grading This section details the updated DXF export and import workflow, focusing on handling graded patterns and curve points in pattern design software. It explains the difference between exporting "standard" DXF files versus graded DXFs and how to manage them when importing back into the software. ### Exporting DXF Files - DXF export supports multiple formats selectable from a dropdown menu. - Users can choose options like graded nest, rule file, and unit measurements (inches). - The export process allows converting curve points, but users can opt to keep curves as-is. - Grading information can be included during export, which affects how patterns and sizes are saved. ### Importing and Managing DXF Files There are two main types of DXF exports to consider: 1. **Graded DXF Export:** - When exporting graded patterns, the software includes all size variations as separate patterns within one DXF file. - Upon import, all graded points and curve points are preserved and visible. - The import dialog offers options like "Optimize All Curve Points" to clean up geometry. - Users typically avoid converting to seam allowance at import to inspect and edit the imported patterns first. - The graded DXF retains grading metadata, allowing easy adjustment and modification of graded points. 2. **Standard DXF Export:** - Exports individual sizes as separate DXF patterns, each named with size identifiers (e.g., "5", "5+84", "5+85"). - Grading is not preserved as metadata; patterns are separate but ungraded. - After import, grading must be manually re-applied: - Select curve points and use "Convert to Graded Point" to assign grading. - Optimize curve points if needed. - This process requires extra steps but provides individual pattern files per size. ### Practical Example - Export two DXF files: one graded and one standard. - Import both into a new project. - The graded DXF imports with all grading intact and optimized curves. - The standard DXF imports as separate patterns for each size with no grading. - Manual grading conversion is required on the standard DXF import to regain graded pattern functionality. ### Recommendations - Use graded DXF export when you want to maintain grading metadata and simplify pattern adjustments. - Use standard DXF export if individual size pattern files are preferred, understanding manual grading assignment will be necessary. - Always check unit settings (e.g., inches) during export and import to maintain scale consistency. --- This update to file import and export presets, especially for OBJ and DXF formats, enhances workflow efficiency by enabling customizable presets and improved handling of graded patterns, supporting diverse production pipelines in 3D modeling and pattern design.
